nodes.summary: Mean fitness is unchanged by one generation of selection exactly when the allele frequencies are at an equilibrium of the selection map.
nodes.title: Mean fitness is unchanged exactly at selection equilibria

nodes.summary: Mean fitness stays positive after one generation of diploid viability selection (for nonnegative frequencies and fitnesses; normalization is not needed).
nodes.title: Mean fitness stays positive under diploid selection

nodes.summary: Mean fitness never decreases under diploid multi-allele viability selection with random mating (Mulholland–Smith 1959; Scheuer–Mandel 1959; Kingman 1961).
nodes.title: Mean fitness never decreases

nodes.summary: Away from equilibria, mean fitness strictly increases under diploid viability selection.
nodes.title: Diploid selection strictly increases mean fitness off equilibria

nodes.summary: Wright's formula (Wright 1937): for two alleles with frequencies `(x, 1 - x)`, one generation of viability selection changes the frequency of allele `0` by `Δx = x (1 - x) (dw̄/dx) / (2 w̄)`. The identity is algebraic and holds for every real `x` with `w̄(x) ≠ 0`; the model domain is `x ∈ [0, 1]` with nonnegative fitnesses.
nodes.title: Wright's formula

nodes.summary: For two alleles with frequencies `(x, 1 - x)`, the mean fitness `w̄(x) = x² w₀₀ + x (1 - x) (w₀₁ + w₁₀) + (1 - x)² w₁₁` has derivative `2 (m₀ - m₁)`, twice the difference of the marginal fitnesses. This holds for every real `x`.
nodes.title: Derivative of two-allele mean fitness

nodes.summary: With nonnegative allele frequencies and genotype fitnesses and positive mean fitness, one generation of selection raises the log mean fitness by at least twice the relative entropy `∑ i, p'_i log (p'_i / p_i)` of the new allele frequencies `p'` from the old ones `p` (Baum–Eagon's argument for the quadratic form `w̄`). nodes.title: Diploid Baum–Eagon mean-fitness inequality, sharp form
